description: The Iowa Distribution Test Systems, from the group of Zhaoyu Wang at Iowa State University, are real distribution grid models paired with one year of smart meter measurements. The first system has 3 feeders and 240 nodes in the Midwest United States and serves 1,120 customers, all with smart meters measuring hourly energy in kWh for 2017; to protect privacy the readings are aggregated at each secondary distribution transformer. The model includes overhead lines, underground cables, substation transformers with tap changers, line switches, capacitor banks and secondary transformers, with the real topology and component parameters. The download page offers a system description, the smart meter data in Excel, an OpenDSS model and MATLAB code for quasi-static time-series simulation, and a second real 296-bus system with the same components. Files are free through Dropbox links; users are asked to cite the 2019 NAPS paper by Bu and colleagues, and no licence is stated. The Opendatasoft hub listing was modified in August 2024. Coverage is utility feeders in the Midwest. Caveats: individual customer loads are not disclosed, and the utility is not named. Simulation uses are validation of power flow, hosting capacity and state estimation methods on a real feeder with field data. Related records: data-columbia-synthetic-grid-western-interconnection is a synthetic transmission test case.
